q: How does the Standard describe business value?
options: The total budget that the sponsor approved in the project charter
The number of features delivered by the end
A net quantifiable benefit, tangible or intangible
The profit made in the first month after launch
explanation: Business value is a net quantifiable benefit in any form of tangible or intangible elements that may contribute to the health of the organization during the project, at its end, or in the long term.

q: A project improves employee well-being and the company's reputation. How does the Standard classify these?
explanation: Figure 2-1 lists employee well-being and reputation among the intangible elements of business value, beside goodwill, brand recognition, public benefit, acquired knowledge and compliance.

q: In MoSCoW prioritization, what does the W stand for?
explanation: MoSCoW buckets items as must have, should have, could have and will not have. It is fast for workshops but coarse-grained and subjective.

q: What is the WSJF calculation in the Agile Practice Guide?
options: Cost of delay multiplied by the size of the job
The size of the job divided by its business value and time criticality
Business value minus the cost of the job
(Business value + time criticality + risk reduction) / size
explanation: Weighted shortest job first is (user business value + time criticality + risk reduction) divided by size. It scales well in backlogs but relies on relative scoring.

q: A backlog item scores 6 for business value, 4 for time criticality and 2 for risk reduction, and its size is 3. What is its WSJF score?
explanation: WSJF = (business value + time criticality + risk reduction) / size: (6 + 4 + 2) / 3 = 4.

q: In the Kano model, how is a feature that customers did not expect but love classified?
explanation: Kano classifies features as basic, performance or delighter. It guides the mix of outcomes but is not a queueing method.

q: Which technique prioritizes work by its time sensitivity and economic impact?
explanation: Cost of delay, including CD3 (cost of delay divided by duration), prioritizes by time sensitivity and economic impact.

q: Which prioritization technique produces one ordered list with no ties and needs a single decision owner?
explanation: Stack rank, or forced ranking, gives one ordered list with no ties. It is clarifying and sparks debate, and needs a single decision owner.

q: What is a weakness of the buy-a-feature technique, according to the Agile Practice Guide?
options: It can be gamed if scope is unclear
It always ranks the cheapest items first
It works only for predictive projects
explanation: In buy-a-feature (the $100 test), stakeholders spend a budget on items. It surfaces true preferences but can be gamed if scope is unclear.

q: Who orders the Product Backlog in Scrum?
explanation: The Product Owner is accountable for Product Backlog management, including ordering Product Backlog items, and for maximizing the value of the product.

q: How much of the backlog does the Agile Practice Guide say should be written before work starts?
options: Every story for the entire project
Enough for the first release broadly and the next iteration
Only the stories for the final release
None at all; stories are written only after the work is delivered
explanation: There is no need to create all the stories before work starts, only enough to understand the first release in broad brushstrokes and sufficient items for the next iteration.

q: Why does the Agile Practice Guide stress shipping increments often?
options: It removes the need for any testing
It lets the team skip the reviews
It keeps the sponsor away from the work
It confirms value and reduces risk
explanation: Shipping confirms value, because only a released increment lets customers decide whether it is worth the investment; it surfaces hidden work; and it reduces risk by revealing problems early.

q: What does the Agile Practice Guide mean when it says frequent shipping "surfaces hidden work"?
options: Packaging, deployment and compliance become visible
Team members' private tasks are reported
Unused budget becomes available to spend
Old requirements are deleted from the backlog automatically each time
explanation: Packaging, deployment, documentation, compliance checks and operational handoffs all become visible when the team ships often.

q: What is the purpose of a minimum viable product?
options: To deliver every single feature before any customer is allowed to see it
To replace the product roadmap with a single release
To learn whether the idea delivers value, with the fewest features
To reduce the project's budget by cutting all testing
explanation: Lean Startup builds the smallest testable version of an idea, the MVP, and runs a build, measure, learn loop with real customer data to confirm the idea or pivot.

q: Which of these is an outcome measure that links delivery to value, in the Agile Practice Guide?
options: Hours logged by each team member
Number of meetings held per week
explanation: Outcome-oriented measures include customer satisfaction or NPS, business value delivered, adoption and usage analytics showing whether released capabilities are used, and time to learn.

q: Who is accountable for monitoring, recording and reporting realized benefits, according to the benefits management plan?
explanation: The benefits owner is the person accountable for monitoring, recording and reporting realized benefits throughout the timeframe established in the plan.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Benefits management plan

q: Which element of the benefits management plan states whether benefits are short term, long term, ongoing or by phase?
options: Strategic alignment with the business strategy
explanation: The plan may include target benefits, strategic alignment, the timeframe for realizing benefits (short term, long term, ongoing or by phase), the benefits owner, metrics, assumptions and risks.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Benefits management plan

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Benefits management plan

q: In the benefits management plan, how may the financial value of target benefits be expressed?
options: As the number of features delivered
explanation: Target benefits are the expected tangible and intangible value; financial value may be expressed as net present value (NPV).
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Benefits management plan

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Benefits management plan

q: Why does the benefits management plan describe how business value becomes part of ongoing operations?
options: Because operations staff write the project charter
Because many benefits are realized after the project closes
Because the plan replaces the operations budget
Because operations staff must approve every single change request raised
explanation: The plans describe how the business value becomes part of the organization's ongoing operations, including the metrics, which verify the value and validate success; many benefits are realized after closure.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Benefits management plan

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Benefits management plan

q: A sponsor wants evidence that a new platform is delivering value, not just features. What should the team show?
options: The number of tasks closed in the tool
The total number of hours the team has worked during this month
The size of the remaining backlog
Outcome metrics such as usage and customer satisfaction
explanation: Stakeholders care about what is delivered and its impact; outcome measures such as adoption and usage, customer satisfaction or business value delivered show value, while counts of tasks or hours show only activity.

q: How can value be assessed, according to the Standard?
options: With measurable metrics or qualitative observations
Only with financial return on investment
Only by counting the number of deliverables completed so far
Only after the product has been retired
explanation: Value can be described and assessed using measurable metrics, such as return on investment, or qualitative observations such as testimonials and societal benefits.

q: When are backlog refinement sessions typically held, according to the Agile Practice Guide?
options: Only once, at the very start of the project, before any iteration
In the middle of the iteration, for upcoming ones
explanation: The product owner works with the team to prepare stories for the upcoming iteration in refinement sessions, typically held in the middle of the iteration.

q: What does the product owner do with the product roadmap as the team delivers?
options: Freezes it, so stakeholders can rely on it
Replans it based on what is produced and new information
Hands it over to the change control board to manage from then on
Deletes it once the first release is done
explanation: The product owner replans the roadmap based on what the team produces and emerging information, creating transparency and alignment on delivering value.

q: Which THREE are backlog prioritization techniques in the Agile Practice Guide?
explanation: Table 5-1 lists MoSCoW, stack rank, value versus effort, cost of delay, WSJF, Kano and buy-a-feature.

q: Which THREE are elements of a benefits management plan?
explanation: The plan may include target benefits, strategic alignment, timeframe, benefits owner, metrics, assumptions and risks to benefits realization.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Benefits management plan

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Benefits management plan

q: Which TWO are reasons the Agile Practice Guide gives for shipping increments?
options: It removes the need for planning
explanation: Shipping confirms value, surfaces hidden work and reduces risk.

q: Match each prioritization technique with how it works.
right: Rank by time sensitivity and economic impact
Stakeholders spend a budget on items
explanation: Table 5-1 of the Agile Practice Guide describes each technique with its strengths and limits.

q: Using the product owner's WSJF scores, which item should go first?
explanation: Seat selection: (9 + 8 + 5) / 4 = 5.5. Mobile tickets: (7 + 6 + 3) / 4 = 4. Donor dashboard: (4 + 2 + 1) / 2 = 3.5. Loyalty points: (6 + 3 + 2) / 5 = 2.2. The highest score goes first.

q: How should the team deliver, to show value before the season starts?
options: Build every requested feature and release them all at once
Release a usable first increment early and gather feedback
Wait for the board to approve a full specification first
Deliver the donor dashboard first, since it is the smallest
explanation: Only a released increment lets customers decide whether the outcome is worth the investment; frequent delivery also reveals problems early. Order follows value, not just size.

q: Who should track the expected 30% cut in box-office costs after launch?
options: The team, until the last iteration ends
A benefits owner named in the benefits plan
Nobody; benefits are checked at closure only
The ticketing software vendor's sales team
explanation: The benefits management plan names a benefits owner accountable for monitoring, recording and reporting realized benefits over the timeframe, with metrics; this benefit arrives after the project ends.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Benefits management plan
